extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry / number theory familiar with IUT and GenEll
extracted.subtask_description: Application of Inter-Universal Teichmüller Theory (IUT) and the GenEll framework to derive diophantine inequalities (in particular ABC / Vojta-type bounds) for elliptic curves and hyperbolic curves, via construction of appropriate initial Θ-data and auxiliary primes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linearization of Logarithms (Prop. 2.1 (i))
rubrics_metrics.description: We have log(x) ≤ x for all real x ≥ 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a basic elementary inequality in subsequent estimates; no further elaboration given (standard calculus inequality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prime number theorem estimate (Prop. 2.1 (ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists a real ξprm ≥ 5 such that for all real x ≥ ξprm the standard θ(x) sums over primes satisfy the stated bounds; in particular, for a finite set A of primes with θA = sum_{p∈A} log(p) there exists a prime p ∈ A with p ≤ 2(θA + ξprm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard analytic number theory estimate is invoked to produce auxiliary primes (e.g., l) with controlled size in terms of log-volumes/heights; references to classical sources and GenEll are given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation: rational points of bounded degree (UX(Q)≤d)
rubrics_metrics.description: UX(Q)≤d ⊆ UX(Q) denotes the subset of Q-rational points defined over a finite extension field of Q of degree ≤ d.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic notation from GenEll used throughout; important for forming finite exceptional sets and measuring dependence on degree d.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalized log-different function (log-diffX)
rubrics_metrics.description: log-diffX denotes the normalized log-different function on UX(Q) (cf. GenEll Definition 1.5 (iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A height-like local conductor/different invariant used in the diophantine inequalities; appears in comparison inequalities (C2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalized log-conductor function (log-condD)
rubrics_metrics.description: log-condD denotes the normalized log-conductor function on UX(Q) (cf. GenEll Definition 1.5 (iv)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used with log-diffX to bound heights/necklaces of points in (C2); appears in explicit inequalities comparing q-invariants and arithmetic invariants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalized height ht_{ωX(D)}
rubrics_metrics.description: ht_{ωX(D)} denotes the normalized height function on UX(Q) associated to the line bundle ωX(D), well-defined up to a bounded discrepancy (cf. GenEll Proposition 1.4 (iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to relate analytic q-parameters to arithmetic heights; appears in equality-of-bounded-discrepancy statements in Corollary 2.2(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric setup for initial Θ-data (X, D, KV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Take X = P^1_Q and D = {0,1,∞}; regard X as the λ-line (Legendre parameter). Let KV ⊆ UX(Q) be a compactly bounded subset whose support contains the nonarchimedean prime 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This concrete choice of base curve and compactly bounded subset is required to construct suitable initial Θ-data that will be used to link elliptic-curve q-parameters to heights; KV and its properties (support, compact-boundedness) are essential hypotheses in Corollary 2.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: j-invariant boundedness condition ((∗j-inv))
rubrics_metrics.description: If v denotes the nonarchimedean prime 2, then the image of the subset Kv ⊆ UX(Q_v) associated to KV via the j-invariant UX → (Mell)_Q → A^1_Q(Q_v) = Q_v is contained in a subset of the form 2^{N_{j-inv}} · O_{Q_v} ⊆ Q_v (i.e., is a bounded subset of Q_v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This local boundedness condition at the nonarchimedean prime 2 is imposed on KV to ensure comparability of q-parameters and to apply the GenEll comparison results; it appears as a hypothesis in Corollary 2.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality of bounded-discrepancy classes relating q-parameters and heights (Cor. 2.2 (i))
rubrics_metrics.description: On KV one has equalities (as bounded-discrepancy classes) among the normalized q-parameter functions and heights: log(q^{(2)}(-)) ≈ (1/6)·log(q_{∀}(-)) ≈ (1/6)·ht_{∞} ≈ ht_{ωX(D)} (with the factor 1/6 arising from degree comparisons).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These proportionality/equality-of-bounded-discrepancy relations let one replace analytic q-invariants by arithmetic heights up to controlled bounded errors when restricting to KV; references to GenEll Proposition 3.4 and Prop.1.4 are given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite exceptional set Excd and uniform bound on log(q_{∀}) (Cor. 2.2 (ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: There exist positive reals Hunif (independent of KV), CK and HK (depending only on KV) such that for given d and an auxiliary small real (denoted (cid:2)d ≤ 1) with δ := 2^{12}·3^3·5·d, there is a finite subset Excd ⊆ UX(Q)≤d (depending only on KV, d, and (cid:2)d), containing points with automorphisms >2, for which the function log(q_{∀}(-)) is ≤ Hunif·(cid:2)^{-3}_d·d^{4+(cid:9)d} + HK on Excd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This asserts the existence of a finite exceptional set controlling large q-values; this exceptional set depends only on KV and degree parameters, and provides the boundedness required to proceed with the main argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field and torsion hypotheses for elliptic curve EF and associated fields (Cor. 2.2 (ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: For an elliptic curve EF over a number field F defining a Q-point lifting to xE ∈ UX(F) ⊆ UX(Q)≤d with xE ∈ KV and xE ∉ Excd, define F_{mod} as the minimal field of definition of the corresponding point in Mell(Q), F_{tpd} = F_{mod}(EF_{mod}[2]) (tripodal intermediate field), assume 3·5 torsion points of EF are defined over F and that F = F_{mod}(√−1, EF_{mod}[2·3·5]) ≅ F_{tpd}(√−1, EF_{tpd}[3·5]). Then EF has stable reduction at every element of V(F)^{non}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These technical field and torsion hypotheses are required to place EF, its torsion structure, and its reductions into the framework of Theorem 1.10 and Proposition 1.8; they ensure the needed control of reductions and fields of definition for later discriminant/conductor comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inequality on auxiliary prime l in terms of log(q_{∀}) (Condition (C1))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the acceptable range for choosing the auxiliary prime l (roughly of order the square root of the height/log-volume). This range is produced using the prime number theorem bound and is central to balancing archimedean/nonarchimedean contributions in the IUT estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison inequality relating q-invariants and arithmetic invariants (Condition (C2))
rubrics_metrics.description: (C2) One has inequalities  (1/6)·log(q) ≤ (1/6)·log(q^{(2)}) ≤ (1/6)·log(q_{∀}) ≤ (1 + (cid:2)_E)·(log-diffX(xE) + log-condD(xE)) + CK , where (cid:2)_E := (60·δ)^2 · log(2·δ·(log(q_{∀})))/(log(q_{∀}))^{1/2}. Also log-diffX(xE) = log(d_{F_{tpd}}) and log(f_{F_{tpd}}) ≤ log-condD(xE) ≤ log(f_{F_{tpd}}) + log(2·l).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the core arithmetic inequality that bounds q-parameters (hence heights) in terms of the log-different and log-conductor (discriminant/conductor) plus an explicit error CK; the parameter (cid:2)_E quantifies a small multiplicative perturbation depending on δ and log(q_{∀}).

rubrics_metrics.name: Refined uniform exceptional set property for smaller thresholds (Cor. 2.2 (iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Hunif may be chosen so that for given d and two small reals (cid:2) and (cid:2)d there exists a finite Exc_{(cid:2),d} ⊆ UX(Q)≤d depending only on KV, (cid:2), d, and (cid:2)d such that log(q_{∀}(-)) ≤ Hunif·(cid:2)^{-3}·(cid:2)^{-3}_d·d^{4+(cid:9)d} + HK on Exc_{(cid:2),d}, and moreover the invariant (cid:2)_E associated to EF satisfies (cid:2)_E ≤ (cid:2) whenever xE ∈ Exc_{(cid:2),d}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a refined exceptional set and a uniform choice of Hunif that enforces the smallness of the perturbation parameter (cid:2)_E on that exceptional set; used to guarantee the effective applicability of (C2) with controlled error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auxiliary prime l existence and properties (P1)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists a prime l satisfying (5 ≤) (log(q_{∀}))^{1/2} ≤ l ≤ 10·δ·(log(q_{∀}))^{1/2}·log(2·δ·log(q_{∀})).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived using Proposition 2.1 and the prime number theorem; furnishes an l of suitable size to input into IUT constructions and later Galois/representation arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-divisibility by l of local multiplicative heights (P2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The chosen prime l does not divide any nonzero local multiplicative height hv for v ∈ V(F)^{non}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures certain local obstructions vanish and is used in controlling the behavior of q-parameters and subgroup schemes; achieved by enlarging the exceptional set if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smallness condition if l equals a bad prime (P3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If l = p_v for some nonarchimedean v with hv nonzero, then one has hv < (log(q_{∀}))^{1/2}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A technical restriction to avoid excessively large local contributions when l coincides with a bad prime; used in the estimates leading to (P5)/(P6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Absence of l-cyclic subgroup scheme (P4)
rubrics_metrics.description: EF does not admit an l-cyclic subgroup scheme (i.e., no l-isogeny cyclic subgroup scheme exists over the relevant base).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is arranged by enlarging the exceptional set; its failure would force log(q_{∀}) to be bounded, producing only finitely many j-invariants, so one can exclude that case for the general argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of a bad multiplicative place in the mod field (P5)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists at least one nonarchimedean valuation in V(F_{mod}) not dividing 2·l at which EF has bad multiplicative reduction (i.e., the set Vbad_{mod} is non-empty).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures inertia/ramification conditions necessary to deduce large Galois image properties for l-torsion and is used to avoid trivial boundedness conclusions; it's enforced by enlarging exceptional sets if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large Galois image on l-torsion (P6)
rubrics_metrics.description: The image of the outer homomorphism Gal(Q/F) → GL_2(F_l) determined by the l-torsion of EF contains SL_2(F_l).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from (P2),(P4),(P5) together with results in GenEll; this 'big image' property is necessary to produce the required arithmetic / monodromy data for IUT initial Θ-data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Θ-data satisfying IUT conditions (P7)
rubrics_metrics.description: One can choose data (F / F, X_F, l, C_K, V, Vbad_{mod}, (cid:2)) such that the conditions (a)–(f) of [IUTchI], Definition 3.1 are satisfied and hence the hypotheses of Theorem 1.10 hold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the culmination: given the previous choices and properties, one obtains initial Θ-data admissible for applying Theorem 1.10; the existence relies on the big-image property (P6) and arrangements of V and (cid:2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome inequality from Theorem 1.10 (application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying Theorem 1.10 yields an explicit inequality of the form log(q) ≤ (1 + δ·h^{-1/2})·(log(d_{F_{tpd}}) + log(f_{F_{tpd}})) + 200·δ^2·h^{1/2}·log(2·δ·h) + 20·ηprm, where h = log(q_{∀}) and other notation as above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives the promised diophantine bound relating q-parameters (hence heights) to discriminant/conductor terms plus explicit error terms; it is the main quantitative step towards ABC/Vojta-type conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifications and conductor inequalities relating geometric and field invariants
rubrics_metrics.description: One has the tautological equality log-diffX(xE) = log(d_{F_{tpd}}) and the inequalities log(f_{F_{tpd}}) ≤ log-condD(xE) ≤ log(f_{F_{tpd}}) + log(2·l).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These comparisons translate between the geometric arithmetic invariants appearing in GenEll notation and the usual field discriminant/conductor terms, and are used to insert conductor/discriminant data into condition (C2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Asymptotic interpretation of the √-height term (Remark 2.2.1 & 2.2.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The error/secondary term of shape δ^{1/2}·log(δ) (and similarly h^{1/2}·log(·)) arises from a balance between archimedean 'δ/l' type terms and nonarchimedean 'l' terms when choosing the auxiliary prime l; this √-term is analogous to phenomena associated with the critical 1/2-line in the Riemann hypothesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This conceptual remark explains the origin of the square-root-height contributions in the quantitative bounds and suggests the qualitative inevitability of such terms in this method; not a formal hypothesis but important guidance for interpreting the bounds.
